breakpoints.note: After `parser_conf_file()` retrieves `format == regex`, `flb_parser_create()` admits the attacker-controlled `regex` property into the vulnerable regex compiler path by calling `flb_regex_create(p_regex)`.
This is the first project statement that turns the witness into vulnerability-relevant parser state: a live `current_section` linked into `cf->parsers`.

For the crashing 9-byte UTF-8 pattern, the final byte `0xec` yields an approximate width of 3 while only one byte remains before `end`, so `PFETCH(c)` moves `p` past the logical regex end. Fixed commit `9cc2ff55a146b2b3e8c321a87920c0d39a2b2ba6` repairs this exact omission by inserting `if (p > end) return ONIGERR_PREMATURE_END_OF_CHAR_CLASS;` immediately after `PFETCH(c);`.

AddressSanitizer reports the crashing project frame as `onig_node_str_cat` and the call chain `onig_node_str_cat -> parse_exp -> parse_branch`. The saved trace does not symbolize the exact copy line inside the function, so this sink anchors the shared copy block at lines 1378-1405. On the staged witness, `str_to_regex()` passed a 9-byte logical payload inside a 26-byte SDS allocation, and the overrun token span extends beyond that 9-byte end. `onig_strcpy(..., s, end)` therefore performs the observed `READ of size 3` on a copy that straddles the payload boundary inside the SDS allocation.
